title: Apple Earnings Live: New CEO John Ternus Faces First Wall Street Test – CNBC Update
body:
Apple’s fourth‑quarter 2026 earnings report, released on Tuesday, delivered a mixed performance that placed its newly appointed chief executive, John Ternus, under the Wall Street spotlight for the first time. The Cupertino giant posted revenue of $90.1 billion, edging up 2 percent year‑over‑year, while earnings per share rose to $1.27, surpassing analysts’ consensus estimate of $1.22. However, the growth was uneven: iPhone sales slipped 3 percent globally, and the company’s China segment posted a steeper 7 percent decline, prompting investors to weigh the impact of Ternus’s strategic pivots and the broader macro‑economic headwinds confronting the tech sector.

The headline numbers were buoyed by robust performance in services and wearables, which together generated $22.9 billion in revenue, a 9 percent jump from the same period last year. Subscription‑based offerings such as Apple Music, iCloud, and the burgeoning Apple TV+ library continued to expand their user bases, reinforcing the firm’s shift toward recurring‑revenue models. Likewise, the Mac and iPad lines showed modest gains, driven in part by the rollout of the M3 chip, which promises higher efficiency and performance for professional users. Analysts noted that these segments helped offset the softness in the flagship iPhone, which still accounted for roughly 54 percent of total revenue.

China, long a cornerstone of Apple’s growth engine, remained a point of concern. The company reported a 7 percent revenue contraction in the Greater China region, reflecting both lingering pandemic‑related supply chain disruptions and intensified competition from domestic manufacturers that have accelerated their own AI‑driven hardware upgrades. Ternus addressed the issue during the earnings call, emphasizing “a renewed focus on localized content, pricing flexibility, and strategic partnerships” aimed at recapturing market share. He also hinted at upcoming product variations tailored to regional preferences, though specifics were not disclosed.

Artificial intelligence, a recurring theme in Apple’s recent product roadmap, featured prominently in the earnings narrative. The firm announced that its next‑generation iPhone will integrate on‑device AI processors capable of handling advanced computational photography, real‑time translation, and personalized health insights without relying heavily on cloud services. This move is intended to differentiate Apple from competitors that lean on external AI platforms, while also addressing growing privacy concerns among consumers. Investors responded positively, with the stock climbing 1.8 percent in after‑hours trading, suggesting confidence that AI integration could reinvigorate the iPhone’s value proposition.

Looking ahead, Apple provided a cautious yet optimistic outlook for the holiday season. The company forecast Q1 2027 revenue in the range of $91 billion to $93 billion, projecting a 3‑5 percent increase year‑over‑year, and expects earnings per share of $1.30 to $1.35. Guidance assumes “steady demand for premium devices” and “continued expansion of services revenue,” while acknowledging potential volatility in global supply chains and foreign‑exchange fluctuations. Market analysts have revised their price targets modestly upward, betting that Ternus’s emphasis on AI‑enhanced hardware and a diversified services portfolio will sustain growth momentum.

In sum, Apple’s Q4 results underscore a transitional phase under John Ternus’s leadership. While the iPhone’s sales dip and China’s slowdown expose vulnerabilities, the company’s expanding services ecosystem and strategic AI investments offer a pathway to resilience. As the holiday shopping season approaches, the true test for the new CEO will be whether these initiatives can translate into sustained top‑line growth and restore investor confidence in the world’s most valuable technology brand. The coming months will reveal if Apple can balance innovation with market realities, setting the tone for its performance throughout 2027.
